en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having one of the most perfect volcanic cones in the world.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the smallest primates in the world with huge eyes.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Laguna de Bay in Luzon is the largest lake in the Philippines and a major source of freshwater fish.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines and is home to the rare Philippine eagle.
Samar is the third-largest island in the Philippine archipelago and is known for its extensive cave systems and waterfalls.
The Philippines is a top global producer of abaca, a strong banana plant native to the country used for making ropes.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral marine life.
The Philippines experiences the amihan, a cool northeast monsoon wind, which brings dry weather to the country from December to February.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous ancestors over 2,000 years ago for farming.
The Waling-waling orchid, native to the rainforests of Mindanao, is highly prized for its beautiful and colorful flowers.
The province of Batanes, the northernmost in the Philippines, features distinct stone houses built to withstand strong Pacific typhoons.
